hero.title: Enterprise-grade security for every business
hero.subtitle: How Jojan One is built, hosted and operated - and what we are still working towards.

items.heading: Where the platform runs
items.body: The Jojan One application is hosted on Vercel. Your business records, accounts and uploaded files are held in Supabase, which provisions managed PostgreSQL on AWS. Our production project is provisioned in a European region.

items.heading: Encryption at rest
items.body: Customer data is encrypted at rest by our infrastructure providers using AES-256. This covers the production database, its automated backups and uploaded files.

items.heading: Encryption in transit
items.body: All traffic is protected using TLS 1.2 or higher. HTTPS is enforced across every endpoint and insecure connections are rejected.

items.heading: Tenant isolation
items.body: Every table is protected by PostgreSQL Row Level Security. Queries run as the signed-in user rather than as a privileged service account, so one workspace cannot read or write another's records even if the application code above it is wrong. Service credentials never reach the browser.

items.heading: Role-based access
items.body: Access inside a workspace is role-based. Every request is checked against the signed-in user's role, the modules their package includes and the workspace they are acting in before any data is returned.

items.heading: Multi-factor authentication
items.body: We require multi-factor authentication on the provider accounts that hold production access, including source control, hosting and the database.

items.heading: Audit logging
items.body: Administrative actions taken in the platform are written to an audit log, alongside a record of platform events, so account changes can be traced after the fact.

items.heading: Isolation testing
items.body: Every data feature ships with an automated test that provisions two separate tenants and asserts that neither can read or write the other's records. These run against a real database rather than a mock, and a feature is not released until its test passes.

items.heading: Dependency management
items.body: We monitor published security advisories for the packages Jojan One depends on and update them as fixes are released.

items.heading: Secure development
items.body: Changes are reviewed before release and must pass an automated type check and the platform's verification suite before they can be deployed to production.

items.heading: Backups
items.body: Our database provider takes automated daily backups of the production database.

items.heading: Incident response
items.body: If a security incident affects personal data we hold on your behalf we will notify you without undue delay, and within 72 hours of becoming aware where UK GDPR requires it.

items.heading: Availability
items.body: We aim for 99.9% monthly availability of the Jojan One platform.

items.heading: Independent penetration testing
items.body: We have not yet commissioned an independent penetration test. Engaging a CREST-accredited assessor, and publishing a summary of the findings and their remediation, is on our roadmap.

items.heading: Certification
items.body: Jojan One does not currently hold ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II or Cyber Essentials Plus. These are the standards we are building towards, and we will say so here when each is achieved rather than before.

items.heading: Status page
items.body: We do not yet publish a live status page. Until we do, service incidents are communicated by email to affected customers.
